claims.text: TUM ProLehre student guidance specifies that generative AI tools may be used for written coursework, term papers, essays, and theses only when AI tool use is explicitly permitted for that specific assessment by the instructor or module specifications. Where no statement regarding AI use is made in the assignment or module handbook, students are strongly advised to ask the instructor in advance; using AI without permission may be treated as attempted deception under APSO § 22 or comparable regulations. When authorized, transparent documentation of tool use and prompts is commonly required, and students retain full personal responsibility for submitted work.

claims.text: In the APSO reading version as amended by the12th amending statute, §22(1) says attempting to influence an examination result through deception or unauthorized aids leads to a failing grade. Suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under §22(2), disruption may lead to exclusion from that examination and a failing grade. In serious or repeated deception or disruption cases, the examination committee may exclude the student from further examinations in the degree program, with final failure of the degree examination (§22(3)). Under §24(6), an examination failed because of §22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. These are general examination provisions, not a separate AI-specific sanction schedule.

claims.text: The Guidelines for Writing Theses and Seminar Papers (Juli 2026) issued by the TUM Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research permit the use of generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) as research aids for seminar, Bachelor's, and Master's theses, subject to mandatory declaration inserted before the bibliography. The declaration requires students to specify the exact tools used and the specific tasks performed (brainstorming, literature search, structuring, code generation, hypothesis generation, translation, image generation, or language improvement), and confirm that they personally reviewed the entire thesis and accept full responsibility. If no AI tools were used, a formal non-use statement must be included ('Ich habe keine generativen KI-Tools oder -Hilfsmittel verwendet.'). AI-generated images must cite the specific tool, and the use of AI for empirical data collection and analysis is prohibited for data protection reasons unless explicitly approved by the thesis supervisor. These are the reviewed chair guidelines; no broader TUM rule established.

topics.evidenceScope: TUM ProLehre 课程作业记录指引与 MKT 教席论文声明要求。

topics.title: 隐私与敏感数据
topics.summary: TUM ProLehre 指引要求师生切勿将个人数据、敏感信息或机密材料输入 AI 工具，该禁令同样适用于 TUM 批准的系统。此外，教学与研习材料（如讲义课件、讲稿、录音录像或历年考题）受知识产权保护，即便利于个人学习目的（如总结、听写或翻译），亦须事先获得授课教师的明确许可方可上传至 AI 工具进行处理。
topics.scope: TUM ProLehre 关于个人数据保护（含已批准工具）及课件教材版权许可的指引。

claims.text: TUM ProLehre guidance instructs students and instructors not to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools, including systems approved by TUM. Prohibited categories include names, matriculation numbers, email addresses, patient records, research participant data, exam data, and confidential research results. Users are instructed to anonymize content prior to entry, utilize generalized or neutral sample texts, and consult instructors or the TUM Data Protection Officer when uncertain.

topics.summary: TUM SGwP 科研规范条例确立了学术诚信标准，要求将科研数据保存在安全持久的介质上，自发表之日起通常保存 10 年，除非具备正当理由缩短期限或适用特定学科标准。MKT 教席指引允许将 AI 作为论文的研究辅助工具，但严禁将 AI 用于实证数据收集与分析，获导师明确批准者除外。
topics.scope: TUM SGwP 科研诚信条例（数据保存）及 MKT 教席论文研究规范。

claims.text: The reviewed TUM-SGwP statute requires researchers working at TUM to follow recognized scientific standards, document work, question results and act honestly (§1). Supervisors must verifiably give the statute to students conducting scientific thesis work (§22). Under §8, primary and evaluated data and evaluation software used for publications must be kept on durable secure media in the originating institution; retention depends on discipline and is ordinarily ten years from the relevant publication, with reasons for non-retention or shorter periods documented. Authorship requires a genuine, traceable contribution and honorary authorship is prohibited (§12). Under §13, scientific misconduct involves knowingly or grossly negligently making false statements, violating others' intellectual property or impairing their research in a scientifically relevant context. Anyone may approach the ombudsperson concerning suspected misconduct (§16).

claims.text: The Guidelines for Writing Theses and Seminar Papers (Juli 2026) issued by the TUM Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research permit the use of generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) as research aids for seminar, Bachelor's, and Master's theses, subject to mandatory declaration inserted before the bibliography. The declaration requires students to specify the exact tools used and the specific tasks performed (brainstorming, literature search, structuring, code generation, hypothesis generation, translation, image generation, or language improvement), and confirm that they personally reviewed the entire thesis and accept full responsibility. If no AI tools were used, a formal non-use statement must be included ('Ich habe keine generativen KI-Tools oder -Hilfsmittel verwendet.'). AI-generated images must cite the specific tool, and the use of AI for empirical data collection and analysis is prohibited for data protection reasons unless explicitly approved by the thesis supervisor. These are the reviewed chair guidelines; no broader TUM rule established.

additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信与纪律程序
additionalTopics.summary: 依所审查的 APSO 阅读整理本，在考试或作业中企图欺骗作弊将导致该考核评定为 5.0（不合格）。因欺骗或扰乱考场而未通过的考试依第 24(6) 条仅可补考一次。依第 25(3) 条，考生可在成绩公布后 1 个月内向考试委员会主席提交附具理由的书面申请查阅试卷档案，具体时间地点由委员会主席与考官共同确定。依第 21 条，考核程序瑕疵必须及时书面提出。正式公布的规程文本较阅读整理本具有法定效力。 此查阅期限并非纪律或行政申诉期限，后者仍未审查。
additionalTopics.scope: TUM APSO 第 22 条不端行为、第 24 条重考、第 25 条查阅试卷档案及第 21 条程序异议规定。

claims.text: In the APSO reading version as amended by the12th amending statute, §22(1) says attempting to influence an examination result through deception or unauthorized aids leads to a failing grade. Suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under §22(2), disruption may lead to exclusion from that examination and a failing grade. In serious or repeated deception or disruption cases, the examination committee may exclude the student from further examinations in the degree program, with final failure of the degree examination (§22(3)). Under §24(6), an examination failed because of §22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. These are general examination provisions, not a separate AI-specific sanction schedule.

claims.text: In the reviewed APSO reading version, §25(3) grants access to written examination work, examiner reports and oral-examination minutes on a reasoned written application after results are announced. The application must reach the examination committee chair within one month of announcement; the chair determines the time and place with the examiner. Under §21, examination-procedure defects must be raised promptly in writing to the committee chair or examiner. This inspection window does not establish a deadline for disciplinary or administrative appeals, which remain unreviewed.

claims.text: TUM ProLehre guidance observes that reliable control of AI use is difficult to impossible and recommends designing assessments so that unauthorized AI use offers no decisive advantage. This is pedagogical guidance; it does not itself determine whether an individual student committed misconduct.

evidence.quote:
Eine zuverlässige Kontrolle der KI-Nutzung ist schwierig bis unmöglich. Wird die KINutzung trotzdem eingeschränkt oder verboten werden, sollten Prüfungen so gestaltet
werden, dass eine unerlaubte Nutzung keinen entscheidenden Vorteil bietet.

additionalTopics.title: 教学指导
additionalTopics.summary: TUM ProLehre 教学指引建议授课教师充分运用其教学自主裁量权，以既定学习成果为出发点决定是否及如何使用 AI，评估 AI 使用是促进、补充还是妨碍核心能力的掌握。指引建议教师确立具备教学依据的课程规则并向学生透明传达预期，同时对学生开展针对性培训，指导其了解 AI 运行原理与局限性、识别偏见与虚假信息并批判性评估 AI 输出。
additionalTopics.scope: TUM ProLehre 教师教学决策指南（第 2 版）；关于学习成果、课程透明度及 AI 能力培训的教学建议。

claims.text: TUM ProLehre guidance states that instructors have broad pedagogical discretion when deciding whether and how AI is used in their courses, and that related rules should be didactically grounded and communicated transparently to students. In student guidance for written coursework (Hausarbeiten, essays, and assessed written work), ProLehre establishes that students are authorized to use AI tools only when AI use is explicitly permitted for that specific assessment.

evidence.quote:
Dozierende an der TUM haben dabei einen großen Entscheidungsspielraum
(siehe TUM AI Strategy). Damit geht zugleich für Sie als Dozierende die Verantwortung einher,
Regelungen didaktisch fundiert zu treffen und für Studierende nachvollziehbar zu kommunizieren.

claims.text: TUM ProLehre guidance recommends starting AI-use decisions from the intended learning outcomes and whether AI use supports, complements, or hinders those competencies.

evidence.quote: Nehmen Sie als Ausgangspunkt für Ihre Entscheidung die angestrebten Lernergebnisse, die Ihre Studierenden in Ihrer Lehrveranstaltung erwerben sollen – und ob der Einsatz von KI das Erreichen dieser Kompetenzen fördert, ergänzt oder behindert.

evidence.location: Schritt 1: Lernergebnisse

claims.text: TUM ProLehre guidance says students often need targeted training in competent AI use, including AI functions, limits, common errors, biases, misinformation, and critical evaluation of AI outputs.

evidence.quote: In vielen Fällen ist es wichtig, Studierende gezielt darin zu schulen, wie ein kompetenter Umgang mit KI aussieht - insbesondere dann, wenn es ein explizites Lernergebnis des Moduls ist. Üben Sie in diesem Fall mit Ihren Studierenden u.a. folgende Aspekte: o o o die Funktionsweise, Grenzen und häufige Fehler von KI benennen und beschreiben, Biases und Fehlinformationen erkennen, sowie KI-Ergebnissen kritisch bewerten und überarbeiten können.
